File No. PS26-27763
Resolution of the City of Tampa, Florida approving Quote Number 11327142 under an existing Purchase Agreement between the City of Tampa and Stryker Sales, LLC for the furnishing of Labor and Travel for Power-Pro ProCare Repair Services in the estimated amount of $20,000 over a 36-month term for use by the Tampa Fire and Rescue Department; authorizing the Mayor to execute said Quote; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. PS26-27763
Resolution of the City of Tampa, Florida approving Quote Number 11327142 under an existing Purchase Agreement between the City of Tampa and Stryker Sales, LLC for the furnishing of Labor and Travel for Power-Pro ProCare Repair Services in the estimated amount of $20,000 over a 36-month term for use by the Tampa Fire and Rescue Department; authorizing the Mayor to execute said Quote; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
Tampa Fire Rescue has standardized the purchase of parts, preventative maintenance, and capital equipment from Stryker Sales, LLC. Standardization to this equipment and these services ensures interoperability, maintenance efficiency, continuity of service, and reduced maintenance costs while avoiding redundancy and additional expenditures associated with implementing and maintaining alternative equipment and services.

This amendment will add Power-PRO ProCare services for travel and labor to the existing standardization. The addition of these services will provide the necessary travel and labor support associated with the maintenance and servicing of Tampa Fire Rescue’s Stryker equipment. The amendment will increase the existing award by approximately $20,000 to accommodate these additional services. It is recommended that the City amend the existing award with Stryker Sales, LLC to include Power-PRO ProCare travel and labor services.

Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement: There is no EBO participation associated with this purchase, as the procurement is being made under a standardization.

File No. PS26-27867
Resolution approving the acceptance of a Voluntary Cooperation Mutual Aid Agreement between the City of Tampa on behalf of the Tampa Police Department ("TPD"), and the Florida Department of Law Enforcement ("FDLE") for the Electronic Surveillance Support Team ("ESST") Multi-Agency Voluntary Cooperation Mutual Aid Agreement; authorizing execution thereof by the Mayor of the City of Tampa; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. PS26-27867
Resolution approving the acceptance of a Voluntary Cooperation Mutual Aid Agreement between the City of Tampa on behalf of the Tampa Police Department ("TPD"), and the Florida Department of Law Enforcement ("FDLE") for the Electronic Surveillance Support Team ("ESST") Multi-Agency Voluntary Cooperation Mutual Aid Agreement; authorizing execution thereof by the Mayor of the City of Tampa; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background: By authority contained in Resolution No. 2025-590, passed and adopted by City Council of Tampa, Florida on July 17, 2025, the City of Tampa on behalf of the Tampa Police Department approved the execution of the Interlocal Agreement for the Tampa Bay Regional Counter-Unmanned Arial Systems (c-UAS) Initiatives.  The Tampa Bay Regional c-UAS Work Group was formed and is operating in a multi-agency effort under the FDLE ESST Task Force to collaborate efforts, joint funding and the sharing of specialized c-UAS equipment and trained personnel.  TPD desires to participate as an agency party in the FDLE ESST Task Force to join the coordinated regional response to protect public safety from from the increased threat posed by unauthorized or malicious use of Unmanned Aerial Systems (“UAS” or “drones”).  The subscribing law enforcement agencies are so located in relation to each other that it is to the advantage of each to receive and extend mutual aid in the form of law enforcement services and resources to adequately respond to continuing, multi-jurisdictional criminal activity, so as to protect the public peace and safety, and preserve the lives and property of the citizens.  The respective law enforcement agencies have the authority under Part 1, Chapter 23, Florida Statutes, “the Florida Mutual Aid Act,” to enter into a voluntary agreement for cooperation and assistance of a routine law enforcement nature that crosses jurisdictional lines.  Tampa Police Department participation will benefit the citizens of the City of Tampa.

agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. PS26-28103 (Part 1 of 2)(See Item 15)
Resolution approving the acceptance of subgrant funding in an amount up to $450,000 from the State of Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT), Highway Traffic Safety Funds, for the Tampa Police Department "Sit Tight and Belt Right" Occupant Protection Program, to promote safety belt and child restraint use through the term of the subgrant ending 9/30/27; authorizing execution thereof by the Mayor of the City of Tampa; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background: Grant funds in an amount up to $450,000 are available to the City of Tampa for use by the Tampa Police Department in the form of a subgrant through a program administered by the State of Florida Department of Transportation under FY 2027 Project Number OP-2027-00208 and Project Title “Sit Tight and Belt Right” Occupant Protection Program.  The City of Tampa desires to accept the awarded subgrant in an amount up to $450,000.  Tampa is below average in safety belt usage and ranks near the top of large cities in the State for occupant-protection related serious injuries and fatalities.  The grant funds, once received and deployed pursuant to the terms of the grant, will help reduce traffic crash fatalities and injuries due to unrestrained or improperly restrained occupants through education and enforcement, and will provide child seats to low income families.  Entering into this agreement is determined to be in the best interest of the City of Tampa.

agendaItems.background:
The Neighborhood Enhancement Department has standardized to Electronic Access to Interests Against Real Property through web-based service Conduits from Net Assets Corporation. Standardization to this service ensures uninterrupted delivery of service as well as reduction of redundancy and costly expenditures for implementation of a new service.

It is recommended that the City purchase Electronic Access to Interests Against Real Property through web-based service Conduits. Being this is a service transaction, a memo was included with an estimated list of services planned to use per year based on previous usage.

Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement: There was no EBO participation, as this purchase is being made under a standardization.

Interests Against Real Property through web-based service Conduits from Net Assets 
Corporation. Standardization to this service ensures uninterrupted delivery of service as well 
as reduction of redundancy and costly expenditures for implementation of a new service. 
It is recommended that the City purchase Electronic Access to Interests Against Real 
Property through web-based service Conduits. Being this is a service transaction, a memo 
was included with an estimated list of services planned to use per year based on previous 
usage. 
Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement: There was no EBO participation, as this 
purchase is being made under a standardization.

FISCAL IMPACT STATEMENT:
That this Resolution shall provide an additional $374,539, subject to annual appropriations, 
for a cumulative amount of $544,539 for use by the Neighborhood Enhancement Department 
within the General Fund.

agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. NCA26-28191
Resolution making certain changes in the budget of the City of Tampa for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; approving the transfer, reallocation, and/or appropriation of $288,458 within the Golf Courses Operations and Golf Courses Capital/Construction Funds; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
The City is required to report the financial operations of its three golf courses, which are managed and operated by the Tampa Sports Authority (TSA). This Resolution provides the necessary revenue and expenditure appropriations to reflect these golf course operations in the City’s annual financial report, as reported by the TSA.

Additionally, capital expenditures for the City’s golf courses are budgeted in the Golf Courses Capital/Construction Fund. Under the City of Tampa’s Capital Assets and Depreciation Policy, any fixed asset costing less than $5,000 or with a useful life of fewer than two years must be classified as an operating expense. Resolution /

Title
A resolution approving a services agreement for persons with intellectual 
disabilities internship administrator services between the City of Tampa, 
Florida and Grow Group, INC. a Florida not for profit corporation to support 
the Mike Phillips All Abilities Internship Program which was designed to 
connect neuro-diverse learners to internship opportunities with the City of 
Tampa in an amount not to exceed twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000); 
authorizing the execution thereof by the mayor of the City of Tampa, providing 
and effective date.
BACKGROUND:
It is in the public interest of the City of Tampa ('City'), to provide services through The Grow 
Group ('Agency') for the residents of the City who are desirous of such services; and pursuant 
to this Service agreement for Persons with Intellectual Disabilities Internship Administrator 
Services ('Agreement') the Agency shall provide greater opportunities for neuro-diverse 
learners to transition more effectively into the workforce by providing internship opportunities 
in selected City departments; and it is the desire of the parties to establish the terms and 
conditions under which the terms of the Agreement shall be implemented; and the term of the 
Agreement is for one year with no guaranteed renewal for subsequent and determined by the 
City; and City shall reimburse the Agency in an amount not to exceed Twenty-Five Thousand 
Dollars ($25,000) for referring eligible persons to intern with the City in different capacities as 
selected and determined by the City; and City Council does hereby affirm that it would be 
beneficial to the residents of the City to enter into this Agreement between City and the 
Agency.
FISCAL IMPACT: Yes
FISCAL IMPACT STATEMENT:
This Resolution approves an agreement between the City of Tampa and the Career Focus, 
Inc. for an amount not to exceed $25,000 to promote the educational and transitional needs 
of students with identified intellectual disabilities through internship opportunities with the City 
of Tampa for the Neighborhood and Community Affairs department within the General Fund.

agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. INF26-27736
Resolution of the City of Tampa, Florida approving a standardization agreement between the City of Tampa and Getinge USA Sales, LLC for the provision of Getinge Autoclave Parts and Service for the Getinge Autoclave, in the estimated amount of $25,939.97, over a 36-month term, for use by the Wastewater Department; authorizing the Mayor to execute said agreement; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
The Wastewater Department has standardized to Getinge Autoclave Parts and Service from Getinge USA Sales, LLC. agendaItems.background:

3. Business Case: This elevator replacement project, at 301 Channelside Drive, improves the quality and longevity of the current elevator system in operation. 6. Community Engagement: The Contract Administration Department (CAD) and Construction, Engineering and Inspection (CEI) division will assist the Contractor in the communication efforts to ensure transparency and integration of the stakeholders.

7. Project: a. Contract delivery method: This is a Design-Build project. A full-time City of Tampa Construction Inspector will be on-site during the project to ensure quality of construction.

b. Placemaking: N/A c. Time, Quality Assurance, Cost Monitoring (Budget) •  _346______ consecutive calendar days.

•  The e-Builder project management software system will be utilized to optimize the monitoring of schedules and costs. This software was recently purchased by the City of Tampa and is a premier system for construction project management.

File No. INF26-28109
Resolution authorizing Change Order 1 Final to Contract 23-C-00004; Yorkshire Watermain Replacement, between the City of Tampa and Dallas 1 Corporation dba Dallas 1 Construction & Development, an increase of $781,022.21 and final payment in the amount of $881,210.88; authorizing the Mayor of the City of Tampa to execute said Change Order on behalf of the City Of Tampa; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
Background:

1. Contract Title: 23-C-00004, Yorkshire Watermain Replacement a. Address of Project: Yorkshire Neighborhood b. Number of bidders/submitters: N/A c. Names of bidders/submitters: N/A d. Dollar amount: $781,022.21 e. Why the awardee was selected: Project was competitively bid with the selection of the apparent low bidder.

2. Contractor/Firm: Dallas 1 Corporation & Development

3. Business Case: Project provided for the furnishing and installation of approximately 10,628 linear feet of 4-inch diameter and 17,127 linear feet of 6 and 8 -inch diameter ductile iron water main with all required appurtenances and fittings including cutting and plugging, roadway and roadside restoration, traffic control, tree protection, grouting of abandoned pipe, valve adjustment and removal, video photography.

This Change Order 1 is the final change order to provide for the release of retainage, overruns, as-built plans, installation of casing, speed humps, meter relocations, maintenance of traffic and mobilizations, and the extension of the contract for 306 additional calendar days.

4. Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement:  Dallas 1 Corporation dba Dallas 1 Construction & Development, the prime contractor, has utilized three (3) City of Tampa-certified firms for subcontracting.

5. Sustainability and Resiliency: This project is consistent with "Transforming Tampa's Tomorrow" Goal of Sustainability and Resiliency and is part of the Water Department's PIPES Program focused on the replacement of aging infrastructure. Approximately five (5.25) miles of water mains will be replaced within the Yorkshire neighborhood area as part of this project.

6. Community Engagement: The CAD Construction, Engineering and Inspection (CAD-CEI) team will assist the Contractor in the communication efforts to ensure transparency and integration of the stakeholders.

7. Project: a. Contract delivery method: This is a Bid project. A full-time City of Tampa Construction Inspector will be on-site during the project to ensure quality of construction.

b. Placemaking: N/A c. Time, Quality Assurance, Cost Monitoring (Budget) • 840 consecutive calendar days.

• The e-Builder project management software system will be utilized to optimize the monitoring of schedules and costs. This software was recently purchased by the City of Tampa and is a premier system for construction project management.

agendaItems.background:
1.Contract Title: 23-C-00014 Athletic Field Lighting Design Build GMP-01 a. Dollar amount: $202,772.69 Decrease, $5,000 final payment b. Why the awardee was selected: Selected Pursuant to FS 287.055 CCNA.

2. Contractor/Firm: Himes Electric Company, Inc

3. Business Case: This lighting project (Project), at multiple city athletic fields, maintains and improves the quality and longevity of the current lighting system in operation. The City of Tampa entered into an agreement with Himes Electric Company, Inc. on September 19, 2024 to provide certain professional design-build services under Contract 23-C-00014 for the Project.

GMP-1 Agreement approved on August 28, 2025, provided construction services to maintain and improve the quality and longevity of the current lighting system at Rowlett Park, Calvin Taylor Park, and Himes Avenue Sports Complex with a Guaranteed Maximum Price in the amount of $1,955,492; GMP 2 Agreement approved on May 21, 2026 provided construction services for at American Legion Park, Gadsden Park, and Perio & Albany Park with a Guaranteed Maximum Price in the amount of $2,253,509.50; Change Order Final to GMP 1 provides for a decrease in the amount of $202,772.69 to GMP 1 revising contracted amount from 1,955,492 to  $1,752,719.31  and authorizes final payment for GMP 1 in the amount of $5,000.00 and establishes a new completion date of August 17, 2026;

4. Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement: Himes Electric Company, Inc., the prime contractor, has utilized one (1) City of Tampa-certified firm for subcontracting.

5.    Sustainability and Resiliency: All new construction for this project shall make the best use of all applicable and sustainable materials and methodologies to reduce operating costs.

6. Community Engagement: The CAD Construction, Engineering and Inspection (CAD-CEI) team assisted the Contractor in the communication efforts to ensure transparency and integration of the stakeholders.

7. Project: a. Contract delivery method: This is a Design-Build project. A full-time City of Tampa Construction Inspector was on-site during the project to ensure quality of construction.

b. Placemaking: N/A c. Time, Quality Assurance, Cost Monitoring (Budget) •   Change Order Final to GMP 1 establishes a new completion date as of August 17, 2026.

•  The e-Builder project management software system was utilized to optimize the monitoring of schedules and costs. This software was recently purchased by the City of Tampa and is a premier system for construction project management.

agendaItems.background:
1. Background: a. Contract Title: 23-C-00003, Cold Milling of Existing Asphaltic Concrete Roadways b. Address of Project: Various locations throughout the City c. Dollar amount:   $124,935.49 d. Why the awardee was selected: Bidder was the lowest responsive and responsible bidders meeting all conditions of the bid The basis of award referred to in Item I-2.11 of Instructions to Bidders shall be the greatest amount of work, which can be accomplished within the funds available as budgeted.

2.Contractor/Firm: Turtle Infrastructure Partners, LLC

3. Business Case: Project provided for cold milling of existing roadways within the City of Tampa as part of the Pavement Management Program. This was a one-year annual contract which was renewed for 2 additional 1 year periods.

Change Order 1 provided for continual services; the contract completion date was changed.

Change Order 2 provided for continual services; the contract completion date was changed.

Change Order 3, Final provides for adjustment of the Contract amount (increase), establishment of the Contract completion date, and with Final Payment to the Contractor.

4. Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement: Turtle Infrastructure Partners, LLC, the prime contractor, has utilized one (1) City of Tampa-certified firm for subcontracting.

5. Sustainability and Resiliency: The project provided for roadway improvements at various locations throughout the City. This project is consistent with Transforming Tampa's Tomorrow goal of Sustainability and Resiliency and is an integral part of the Pavement Management Program.

6. Community Engagement: The Mobility Public Relations staff assisted the Contractor in the communication efforts to ensure transparency and integration of the stakeholders.

7. Project: a. Contract delivery method: This is a Design-Bid- Build project. A full-time City of Tampa Construction Inspector will be on-site during the project to ensure quality of construction.

b. Placemaking: N/A c. Time, Quality Assurance, Cost Monitoring (Budget) •  0 consecutive calendar days.

•  The e-Builder project management software system was utilized to optimize the monitoring of schedules and costs. This software was recently purchased by the City of Tampa and is a premier system for construction project management.

agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. INF26-28139
Resolution rescinding Resolution 2026-636 passed and adopted on August 6,2026 and authorizing an Amendment to the Agreement for Consultant Services between the City of Tampa and HNTB Corporation regarding Contract 24-D-00034-CSA01 Regional Infrastructure Accelerator in the amount of $999,800; authorizing the Mayor to execute said Amendment on behalf of the City of Tampa; providing for funding thereof; and providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
1. Contract Title: 24-D-00034-CSA01 Regional Infrastructure Accelerator a. Address of Project: Citywide b. Number of bidders/submitters: N/A c. Names of bidders/submitters: N/A d. Dollar amount: $999,800.00 e. Why the awardee was selected: In compliance with requirements of Section 287.055, Florida Statues Consultants Competitive Negotiation Act.

2. Contractor/Firm: HNTB Corporation

3. Business Case: It is necessary to rescind Resolution 2026-636 adopted August 6,2026 to incorporate language in the Amendment referencing certain Federal Execute Orders, as requested by the U.S. Department of Transportation.

The project provides for maintaining and updating a work plan to ensure effective coordination, communication, and analysis, supporting the City in implementing the Regional Infrastructure Accelerator Project (Project).

Services will include project management and cost controls, including: • Coordinating requirements with the City and project team.

• Establishing and maintaining a cost control system to process, track, and report project costs, including invoicing and payments.

• Preparing invoices with narrative descriptions of project progress and task completion.

• Conducting bi-weekly check-ins with the City and the Tampa Bay Partnership to review project progress.

Amendment 1 provides for an analysis to support planning and investment decisions by identifying how asset concessions and dispositions can enhance land value, attract developers, and align with City transportation and development goals. Services will include, but not be limited to: • Assessing the development potential of City assets.

• Evaluating the role of concessions and dispositions in catalyzing development.

• Evaluating the role of concessions and dispositions in generating new revenue streams.

• Analyzing market conditions and comparable Transit Oriented Development (TOD) and other real estate projects.

• Recommending concession and disposition strategies that align with public policy and economic development, and transportation investment goals. Concession strategies may include, but are not limited to public-private partnerships, asset monetization, and joint development.

4. Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement: HNTB Corporation, the prime contractor, is utilizing no City-certified SLBE firms for subcontracting related to Amendment 1.

5. Sustainability and Resiliency: An initial assessment of pending projects across the Tampa Bay Region will be conducted to develop a “long list of projects” (“Long List”) for project pipeline evaluation.

6. Community Engagement: Through an iterative stakeholder outreach and consultation process, additional projects for screening may be identified and incorporated into the Long List.

7. Project: a. Contract delivery method: This is a Design RFQ project.

b. Placemaking: This project aims to evaluate the strategic use of concessions and dispositions to stimulate development on or generate revenue from undeveloped/underutilized assets owned by the City of Tampa (City).

c. Time, Quality Assurance, Cost Monitoring (Budget) • 300 consecutive calendar days.

• The e-Builder project management software system will be utilized to optimize the monitoring of schedules and costs. This software was recently purchased by the City of Tampa and is a premier system for construction project management.

Substitute resolution of the City Council of the City of Tampa, Florida, approving Standard Grant Agreement No. VW507 between the City of Tampa and the State of Florida Department of Environmental Protection for acceptance of grant funds in the amount of $800,000 to purchase solid waste trucks; authorizing execution by the Mayor and attestation by the City Clerk; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
The City of Tampa has applied for grant funding in the amount of $800,000 from the State of Florida Department of Environmental Protection for the Class 8 Municipal Service Trucks Project. The State of Florida Department of Environmental Protection has approved the City of Tampa’s application for funding for the Class 8 Municipal Service Trucks Project, and the City of Tampa desires to accept the awarded grant.

The grant funds will be used for the purchase of two new Class 8 trucks to replace higher-emitting diesel Class 8 trucks. This Grant Agreement requires the Grantee to complete four tasks.

Task 1, the Grantee will identify the existing eligible diesel trucks that the Grantee proposes to scrap and submit specific information to the Department on Worksheet 1 (Diesel Truck Eligibility Certification) for the Department’s review and approval.

Task 2, the Grantee will purchase and receive delivery of new trucks.

Task 3, the Grantee will complete the scrapping process and submit a completed Worksheet 2 (Certificate of Truck Engine and Chassis Destruction) for each scrapped truck.

Task 4, the Grantee will submit to the Department documentation of the purchase and receipt of the new trucks, including a photo of each new truck, an invoice for each truck, proof of payment for each truck, a Summary Detail Spreadsheet, and a completed and signed Exhibit B Property Reporting Form.

There is a required grantee match of $119,215.46 for a total project cost of $919,215.46.

Title
A resolution of the City Council of the City of Tampa, Florida, relating to the 
Florida Department of Environmental Protection (“FDEP”) State Revolving 
Fund (“SRF”) program; approving the Water Facilities Plan and Business Plan 
for the Hillsborough River Reservoir Dam Remediation Project; providing an 
effective date.
BACKGROUND:
To secure a $20 million state loan and grant package for the Hillsborough River Reservoir 
Dam Remediation project, City Council’s approval of the Water Facilities Plan and Business 
Plan is required by November 15. Half of the $20 million funding is forgiven as a grant, while 
the remaining $10 million is an interest-free loan (with a $400,000 service fee) to be repaid 
using water system revenues, helping cover the project's total estimated $38.9 million 
construction cost.
FISCAL IMPACT: Yes
FISCAL IMPACT STATEMENT:
This resolution authorizes the City to submit the Facilities Plan and Business Plan through the 
Florida Department of Environmental Protection’s State Revolving Fund Program for project 
financing of $20 million with a 50% principal forgiveness provision, such that one-half of the 
principal amount of the loan will not be required to be repaid by the City. The interest rate is 
0% with a 2% one-time service fee. The City’s water system has sufficient net revenues to 
service the projected annual debt service for a term of 20 years. The final annual debt service 
will be calculated upon completion of the financed projects and final closing of the loan.

File No. F26-28233
Resolution of the City Council of the City of Tampa, Florida, superseding all previous resolutions regarding the schedule of wastewater disposal charges for all City of Tampa wastewater customers within the City of Tampa’s service area; adopting new wastewater monthly base charges and wastewater disposal rate charges; providing an effective date.
Memorandum from Rory Jones, P.E., Water Department Director, notifying Council that staff will be present to present; and transmitting a PowerPoint presentation for said agenda item. (To be R/F)
agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. F26-28233
Resolution of the City Council of the City of Tampa, Florida, superseding all previous resolutions regarding the schedule of wastewater disposal charges for all City of Tampa wastewater customers within the City of Tampa’s service area; adopting new wastewater monthly base charges and wastewater disposal rate charges; providing an effective date.
Memorandum from Rory Jones, P.E., Water Department Director, notifying Council that staff will be present to present; and transmitting a PowerPoint presentation for said agenda item. (To be R/F)
agendaItems.background:
The City of Tampa provides wastewater collection services to customers both within the city and in surrounding areas outside the municipal limits. Recently enacted Chapter 2026 135, Laws of Florida, which takes effect July 1, 2027, amends section 180.191, Florida Statutes, and changes how municipalities may apply surcharges to customers located outside their boundaries. To ensure compliance with these new statutory requirements, and under the authority of Section 26 31 of the City of Tampa Code of Ordinances, the City has determined that updates to its wastewater monthly base charges and disposal rates are necessary.

Additionally, in 2019 the City conducted a comprehensive Rate Study to identify the funding needed to support implementation of the Wastewater Master Plan.

As of July 1, 2027, the City is unable to continue adding the 25% surcharge to the bills of non-City customers.  The proposed wastewater disposal rates schedule increases City residents’ rates by 9% and decreases non-City customer rates by 16%. The proposed wastewater base charges schedule reduces the base charges for non-City customers so that non-City customers pay the same base charges as City customers. The recommended rate schedules will become effective on July 1, 2027.  Failure to adopt the proposed wastewater disposal rate and base charges schedules will result in lost wastewater revenues of approximately $12 million annually.

agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. F26-28240
Resolution of the City Council of the City of Tampa, Florida, superseding all previous resolutions regarding the schedule of water connection fees, not including reclaimed water rates, for all City of Tampa water customers within the City of Tampa service area; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
The City of Tampa provides potable water service to customers within the City’s service area, which includes customers beyond the City’s municipal boundaries.  Chapter 2026-135, Laws of Florida, amends section 180.191, Florida Statutes, (effective July 1, 2027), which modifies a municipality’s authority to impose a surcharge on customers outside of a municipal boundary. Pursuant to the authority in Section 26-31 of the City of Tampa Code of Ordinances, the City has determined that it is necessary to revise its water connection fees to comply with section 180.191, Florida Statutes.

As of July 1, 2027, the City is unable to continue adding the 25% surcharge to water connection fees paid by non-City customers. The proposed water connection fees schedule eliminates the surcharge so that non-City customers pay the same water connection fees as City customers. The recommended rate schedules will become effective on July 1, 2027.

Failure to adopt the proposed water connection fee schedules will result in lost water revenues of approximately $80,000 annually.

agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. DEO26-27674
Resolution approving a Software Service and Licensing Agreement between the City of Tampa and City Wise Software LLC (“City Wise”) for a housing software platform to list available rental properties within the City of Tampa; authorizing the Mayor to execute said agreement; providing an effective date.
Memorandum from Robert Scott, Housing and Community Development Director, transmitting additional information for said agenda item. (To be R/F)
agendaItems.background:
The Housing and Community Development (HCD) Department assists residents in locating affordable rental housing and connecting them with available housing resources. Currently, rental housing information is available through various sources.  However, those sources are not always current, may not allow users to easily filter available units based on income eligibility or other housing considerations, and may include properties located outside the city limits of Tampa.

The proposed agreement with City Wise Software LLC will provide a web-based rental housing portal accessible through the City's HCD website. The portal will consolidate rental listings from multiple sources into one location and provide search tools to help residents identify available housing, including units that may be affordable to income-qualified households and households utilizing housing vouchers.

CityWise will host, maintain, support, and update the rental housing portal. The platform will provide direct links and contact information for available rental listings and will integrate with commonly used property-management systems to assist with keeping listing information current. CityWise will also review listings included on the site.

CityWise currently operates in more than 20 cities across the country, including St.

Petersburg, Florida, as well as other municipalities of comparable size.

The portal will serve as an additional resource for residents and HCD staff and is intended to improve access to rental housing information while reducing the time required to search multiple sources for available units.

There is no fiscal impact to the City associated with this agreement. CityWise will provide the platform at no licensing or subscription cost to the City.

limits of Tampa.
The proposed agreement with City Wise Software LLC will provide a web-based rental 
housing portal accessible through the City's HCD website. The portal will consolidate rental 
listings from multiple sources into one location and provide search tools to help residents 
identify available housing, including units that may be affordable to income-qualified 
households and households utilizing housing vouchers.
CityWise will host, maintain, support, and update the rental housing portal. The platform will 
provide direct links and contact information for available rental listings and will integrate with 
commonly used property-management systems to assist with keeping listing information 
current. CityWise will also review listings included on the site. 
CityWise currently operates in more than 20 cities across the country, including St. 
Petersburg, Florida, as well as other municipalities of comparable size.
The portal will serve as an additional resource for residents and HCD staff and is intended to 
improve access to rental housing information while reducing the time required to search 
multiple sources for available units. 
There is no fiscal impact to the City associated with this agreement. CityWise will provide the 
platform at no licensing or subscription cost to the City.
FISCAL IMPACT: No

(dba Visit Tampa Bay) on behalf of the Tampa Bay Trade & Protocol Office for the performance of certain protocol and diplomatic services by the Tampa Bay Trade & Protocol Office for an amount not to exceed $48,000 during the 2027 Fiscal Year; Authorizing execution by the Mayor and attestation by the City Clerk; Providing an effective date.
agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. DEO26-28161
Resolution approving an Agreement between the City of Tampa and the Tampa Bay Convention and Visitors Bureau, Inc. (dba Visit Tampa Bay) on behalf of the Tampa Bay Trade & Protocol Office for the performance of certain protocol and diplomatic services by the Tampa Bay Trade & Protocol Office for an amount not to exceed $48,000 during the 2027 Fiscal Year; Authorizing execution by the Mayor and attestation by the City Clerk; Providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
The City of Tampa and Tampa Bay Trade & Protocol Office have partnered since 2012. The agency will be utilizing the FY2027 $48,000 funding to support their work with consuls, ambassadors and diplomatic trade commissioners in enhancing investment and trade opportunities within the Tampa Bay region. Staff from the Tampa Bay Trade & Protocol Office support top public officials, such as the Mayor, City Council Chair, and the Chair of the County Commission, in communications with high-level delegations of international business and government organizations. The Tampa Bay Trade & Protocol Office also partners with Tampa Sister Cities, USF World, Bi-National Chambers, and the United States Global Leadership as an advisory member for the State.

The Tampa Bay Trade & Protocol Office has facilitated outbound missions to approximately 19 countries in the past five years. In FY2026 (Q1-Q3), the Tampa Bay Trade & Protocol Office assisted as follows: Consular Corps Meetings: 10 Inbound Dignitary Visits: 5 Outbound Delegations: 1 Protocol Training: 2 Bi-National Meetings: 2

SubjectAn Ordinance granting to Robles Park, LLC, Robles Park Village Development 
Group, LLC, RPV Parcel D, L.P., its successors and assigns, a non-exclusive 
franchise to use a portion of North Avon Avenue, in the City of Tampa.
Resolution / 
Ordinance 
Title
An Ordinance granting to Robles Park, LLC, Robles Park Village Development 
Group, LLC, RPV Parcel D, L.P., its successors and assigns, a non-exclusive 
franchise to use a portion of North Avon Avenue, in the City of Tampa to 
construct, access and maintain stormwater improvements and prescribing the 
terms and conditions under which said non-exclusive franchise may be 
exercised; providing for severability; providing an effective date.
BACKGROUND:
The City and Robles Park, LLC, Robles Park Village Development Group, LLC, and Open 
Space Acquisitions, LLC (collectively, the “Developer”) entered into a Development 
Agreement, dated September 5, 2024, regarding the development of property located on N. 
Central Avenue, Tampa, Fl (“Development Agreement”).  As part of the development, a 
private stormwater pipe will be crossing North Avon Avenue, which is a public right of way. 
The Development Agreement requires that the Developer obtain a franchise from the City in 
order to allow the stormwater pipe to cross the right of way.
FISCAL IMPACT: Yes
FISCAL IMPACT STATEMENT:
This ordinance approves an agreement between the City of Tampa and Robles Park, LLC, 
Robles Park Village Development Group, LLC, and Open Space Acquisitions, LLC to use a 
portion of the right of way located within North Avon Avenue to construct, access, and 
maintain Stormwater Improvements. The City will collect a franchise fee in the amount of 
$2,500 in FY2027, with a 3% annual increase over a 20 year period for a total of $67,175.94. 
These funds will be collected by the Stormwater Department and deposited within the 
Stormwater Service Assessment Fund.
